messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The test `testEqualsCS2` in `StringUtilsTest` is failing on assertion `Assert.assertFalse(StringUtils.equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), "abcd"))`. The failing bug report indicates that the method `equals(CharSequence cs1, CharSequence cs2)` can throw a String Index Out Of Bounds Exception (OBE) if the two `CharSequence`s have different lengths.  

Looking at the `StringUtils.equals` method implementation, it calls `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(cs1, false, 0, cs2, 0, Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length()))` to perform the comparison. The bug report points to a failure when the sequences have different lengths. The length parameter used here is `Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length())`. This means `regionMatches` is asked to compare up to the maximum length of the two sequences.  

Inspecting `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches`, the method performs character comparisons in a while loop up to the given `length`. It uses `charAt(index1++)` and `charAt(index2++)` calls without any explicit bounds check inside the loop. If `length` exceeds the length of either `cs` or `substring` objects being compared, calling `charAt` with out-of-bound index will cause a String Index OBE.  

Since `StringUtils.equals` uses the maximum length of both inputs without checking if both inputs are at least that long, it enables the `regionMatches` method to attempt accessing indices beyond the length of the shorter sequence which throws the exception. This explains why `equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), "abcd")` throws an exception instead of returning false. The shorter input "abc" has length 3, and the longer "abcd" length 4, so `regionMatches` tries to compare 4 characters resulting in an out of bounds access on "abc".  

Hence the root cause is a length calculation error in `StringUtils.equals` where it should use the minimum length instead of the maximum length of the two sequences to avoid out-of-bounds access in the `regionMatches` call.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report, the failing test behavior, and the code behavior. The recent bug reports are unrelated to the root cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
